# Chuck the 4awardhelper

Chuck the 4awardhelper reviews pending nominations on `Wikipedia:Four Award`.
It is designed to run as a Toolforge scheduled module job under Chuck the
Buckbot Framework.

The supported schedule invokes the manifest handler through `module_runner`.
A legacy compatibility route remains at
`GET /four_award/api/v1/four_award/cron/run`; it has no authentication/token,
runs synchronously, and bypasses framework run tracking and runtime config. Do
not use or expose it as an operational trigger.

## What It Does

- Reads the current Four Award nomination section.
- Verifies article creation, DYK, GA, and FA evidence.
- Produces a dry-run report with proposed edits and verification details.
- Builds a local SQL-backed model of the records table for duplicate checks,
  sorting, and full-table preview output.
- Optionally removes reviewed nominations, updates records, marks article
  history, and posts user-talk notices.

## Recommended Operating Mode

Keep `dry_run` enabled while testing new parser or verifier behavior. Use the
module run page to queue historical-diff tests against older versions of
`Wikipedia:Four Award`; historical tests intentionally skip duplicate-record
checks because current records would otherwise make old nominations fail.

When a dry run would approve a nomination and add a record, the run output
includes a preview of the rebuilt records table. Review that preview before
enabling live records writes.

The run list defaults to unique historical claims so repeated tests against the
same nomination are easier to scan. Clear the unique-only checkbox to inspect all
stored runs, and use the load-more control to page deeper into history.

## Important Settings

Framework runtime config takes precedence during managed runs. The package's
`FOUR_AWARD_*` environment values are defaults for compatibility and standalone
execution, not a second production control plane.

- `enabled`: Stop the module handler without changing the framework registry.
- `wiki_code`: MediaWiki language/site code, usually `en`.
- `wiki_family`: Pywikibot family, usually `wikipedia`.
- `wiki_api_url`: MediaWiki API endpoint for historical revision fetches.
- `four_page`: Nomination page, usually `Wikipedia:Four Award`.
- `records_page`: Records table page.
- `dry_run_report_page`: Optional userspace report page.
- `publish_dry_run_report`: Publish dry-run report to userspace when true.
- `max_nominations_per_run`: Bound work in one scheduled pass.
- `enable_replies`, `enable_records`, `enable_removal`,
  `enable_talk_notices`, and `enable_article_history`: Independently permit
  each write category when the run is not dry.
- `allow_automated_approval`: Allow fully verified nominations to be processed
  without manual intervention.
- `ignore_existing_records` and `award_date_override`: Test/replay controls;
  leave unset for normal scheduled operation.
- `edit_summary_suffix` and `brfa_task`: Reviewed edit attribution text.

## Module Rights

- `module:four_award:view`: View 4award runs and dry-run output.
- `module:four_award:run_jobs`: Queue historical dry-run tests and module jobs.
- `module:four_award:edit_config`: Edit non-secret module settings.
- `module:four_award:manage`: Manage the module.
- `module:four_award:estop`: Emergency-stop the module; generated by the
  framework.

Framework `view_all` also grants module job viewing.

`view` and `estop` are generated by the framework for every module. The module
manifest declares only module-owned worker/config rights.

## Frontend Ownership

The Vue app for this page lives in this module repository under
`modules/four_award/frontend`. Build it with:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

The module build outputs packaged assets under `modules/four_award/static`, but
the current manifest sets `bundled = true`. The framework therefore compiles
the vendored `frontend/entry.ts` through its root Vite registry instead of
serving those package assets. A sibling module build alone does not change the
framework UI; refresh the vendored snapshot or use a temporary sibling-source
registry import for local iteration.
